blocks.summary: The abstract introduces replay-free visual revisiting and PRCR's position rebinding solution.
The introduction motivates visual revisiting, explains token replay cost, and diagnoses direct KV reuse collapse.
The method defines standard MCoT, interleaved reasoning, RoPE-bound visual keys, RVEM, PCR, and replay-free cache decoding.
The experiment section defines benchmarks, model backbones, baselines, and quantitative comparisons.
Ablations compare reinsertion strategies, left extension length, and computational efficiency.
Qualitative figures show corrected visual revisiting, stabilized generation, and cleaner attention.
Related work covers multimodal chain-of-thought, visual grounding, and efficient multimodal inference.
The conclusion states the limitation around new local zoom or dynamic-resolution evidence and future multi-scale rebinding directions.
Figure 1 motivates PRCR and shows accuracy and FLOPs comparisons.
Figure 2 shows decoding collapse under direct historical KV reuse.
Figure 3 visualizes attention perturbation under direct historical KV reuse.
Figure 4 gives an overview of PRCR with RVEM, position reassignment, and replay-free cache decoding.
Algorithm 1 describes PRCR execution; it is described in prose because the extracted crop is very small.
Table 1 compares PRCR with baseline and Token-Replay across four MLLMs and four benchmarks.
Table 2 ablates Direct KV Reuse, LPA, UIR, and PCR position strategies.
Figure 5 shows that left extension length L=2 works best.
Table 3 reports visual-revisiting FLOPs and memory overhead.
Figure 6 shows a ruler/twig example where PRCR revisits evidence and answers correctly.
Figure 7 shows higher next-token probability and lower entropy after PRCR insertion.
Figure 8 compares attention under Token-Replay and PRCR.
